needs: The exact error payload shape sent by the friend server for stream-level errors.
The call-site handling of askFriend rejections to know how abort errors are consumed.
The actual legacy API key file location and whether the legacy config ever contained a keyFile field.
spurious: major: loadFriends/readKey and DEFAULTS — The legacy single-friend config fallback does not fall back to the legacy API key file path.

answers.claim: The fetch error handler only checks the timeout signal, so a caller abort is misclassified and wrapped as a connectivity error.
answers.test: Abort the signal during a pending fetch to /chat/completions; expect askFriend to reject with an abort error, but the current code rejects with the cannot-reach message.

answers.claim: The legacy single-friend config fallback does not fall back to the legacy API key file path.
answers.test: Create a legacy config and key under ~/.config/pi-escalation/ with no new config, then read the friend key; expect the legacy key content, but the current code reads the new key path.

answers.claim: The SSE parser ignores error events and does not surface stream-level errors.
answers.test: Fake SSE server sends a final data event containing an error object; expect askFriend to reject with that error, but the current code resolves with an empty answer.

needs: Whether the runtime supports AbortSignal.any, since the code relies on it.
How the caller surfaces errors from askFriend when the abort signal fires.

answers.claim: The timeout is configured as cfg.timeoutMin * 1000 milliseconds, but timeoutMin is documented and named in minutes, so a 20-minute budget becomes a 20-second timeout.
answers.test: Set timeoutMin to 1 and stall the SSE stream; the current code times out after about 1 second, while the fixed code should allow about 60 seconds.

answers.claim: The queue does not serialize concurrent tasks: pending is decremented synchronously and tail is not awaited, so multiple run calls can start immediately.
answers.test: Call queue.run(task1) and queue.run(task2) without awaiting, with task1 delayed; assert task2 starts only after task1. The current code starts task2 immediately and fails this ordering assertion.

answers.claim: When the caller aborts, the catch checks only the standalone timeout signal, not the combined signal, so the error is reported as an unreachable server instead of a clean abort.
answers.test: Abort the caller signal during a stalled stream; assert askFriend rejects with an abort-related error or that the error is not the reachability message. The current code fails the message assertion.
